national_raw_news.title: Home Minister Amit Shah meets families of those killed for raising voice against drug menace in P...
national_raw_news.content: Union Home Minister Amit Shah today met the family members of those who had been killed in Punjab’s Mansa and Gurdaspur recently for raising their voices against the drug menace in the state. During his day-long visit, he also met the family of Gulzar Singh, who had committed suicide allegedly when his pleas were not heard by the state government against the sale of drugs, which made his son a drug addict. Later, briefing the media in Ludhiana, the Home Minister said that the situation of the family members has shaken him. He blamed the Aam Aadmi Government in Punjab for protecting the drug traffickers. He said that gangs are working in districts to protect drug traffickers. He told Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann that he would not be able to handle the other two cases also and would hand them over to the CBI as well. Akashvani Jalandhar Correspondent reports that the Home Minister promised Punjab that the case of Parvinder Singh Jhota, which the Chief Minister handed over to the CBI, will be thoroughly taken care of and none involved in this episode will be spared. He assured us that by December 2029, Punjab will be drug-free, and those involved will be put behind bars. Jhota was shot dead by a chemist, Ashwani Kumar, in Mansa when he objected to the sale of synthetic drugs by the chemist. His family has not yet cremated his mortal remains even after a week of his murder till justice is delivered. Later, Mr Shah participated in the Dussehra ceremony at Ludhiana, where the burning of Ravana’s effigy has symbolically been themed as ‘Ravan of Chitta.’ During his address, he assured that by the end of 2029, the ‘Ravana of Drugs’ will also be burnt to free Punjab from drugs

national_raw_news.title: EAM S Jaishankar holds trilateral meeting with UAE Foreign Minister Abdullah bin Zayed and US Sec...
national_raw_news.content: External Affairs Minister Dr S. Jaishankar held a trilateral meeting with UAE Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Sheikh Abdullah bin Zayed Al Nahyan and US Secretary of State Marco Rubio in Mumbai today. In a social media post, Dr Jaishankar described the meeting as a useful exchange of perspectives on energy, connectivity and contemporary developments. Dr Jaishankar also held talks with Mr Rubio. The two Ministers exchanged views on strengthening India-US ties, focusing on trade, energy, technology, defence and people-to-people ties. They also discussed regional issues, including the West Asia crisis. Earlier today, Dr Jaishankar met UAE Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Sheikh Abdullah bin Zayed Al Nahyan. Speaking on the occasion, Dr Jaishankar said that despite global headwinds and regional challenges, the India-UAE economic partnership continues to set new benchmarks. He noted that bilateral trade has crossed 100 billion US dollars since the signing of the Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA). Dr Jaishankar added that two-way investments continue to grow, reflecting the confidence businesses in both countries have in each other’s economies. He said cooperation in defence, energy and technology is acquiring a strategic character, while people-to-people ties continue to enrich the lives of communities in both countries.

national_raw_news.content: The festival of Dussehra, which marks the triumph of good over evil, is being celebrated across the nation today. Gracing Dussehra clebrations at IP Extension in the national capital, Prime Minister Narendra Modi hoped that all the institutions of the nation and all political parties stand united for national interest. He said people must stand united to confront the enemies of the nation. He said those who seek to harm the nation’s honor, divide society, and harbor hatred for Indian culture are the enemies of the country. He said nation should reaffirm resolve to identify the enemies of India and defeat them. Mr. Modi said that Vijaya Dashami celebrates the victory of good over evil and reminds everyone of the enduring strength of truth and righteousness. He said, Lord Ram faced many problems in his life but always stood with truth and principles. Mr Modi said, Lord Ram’s life story gives the message of compassion, love and brotherhood. He highlighted that his government also wants to bring Ram Rajya with good governance, as nation moves towards the goal of Viksit Bharat. President Droupadi Murmu graced Dussehra celebrations at Dwarka in Delhi this evening. Speaking on the occasion, President Murmu extended her greetings to the nation. She said that through Ram Leelas organised across the world, many people remember the principles and values of Lord Ram. She said people can learn the importance of conservation of environment and nature through Lord Ram’s life. Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta was also present on the occasion.

national_raw_news.title: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh calls for unified action to dismantle ecosystem of terrorism at SC...
national_raw_news.content: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh today emphasised that connectivity must be based on consultation and respect for the sovereignty and territorial integrity of all countries. Addressing the 25th Meeting of the Council of Heads of Government of SCO in Dushanbe, Tajikistan, the Defence Minister emphasized the importance of connectivity for shared prosperity. He added that projects not founded on these principles will not be sustainable. He stated that India supports initiatives that link markets, facilitate trade and create new avenues for development. He said that initiatives such as the International North-South Transport Corridor and the Chabahar Port can contribute significantly to connecting Central Asia with broader markets. Mr Singh stressed that SCO’s success lies in creating opportunities for youth, entrepreneurs, farmers and small businesses. He asserted that India’s own development experience demonstrates the transformative potential of technology and innovation that drive growth and deliver solutions. He highlighted the country’s Digital Public Infrastructure, which has transformed public service delivery and enhanced financial inclusion. He added that India has built one of the world’s largest start-up ecosystems. He further said that the nation’s emphasis on women-led development is rooted in the belief that women play a defining role in shaping the path of development. The Defence Minister called for unified action to dismantle the entire ecosystem of terrorism. Mr Singh stressed that there can be no justification for terrorism, no double standards in addressing it, and no place for those who finance, support, or provide safe havens to terrorists. The Minister underscored India’s belief that economic engagement should be inclusive and mutually beneficial for all Member States. He said, SCO must remain efficient and steadfast in its adherence to the principles of sovereign equality, consensus, and mutual respect. Mr Singh emphasised the need for the SCO to build consensus and translate it into concrete action to address the uncertain global economic environment marked by geopolitical tensions, disruptions to trade and supply chains, concerns over energy and food security, and emerging technological divides. He stressed on the need to strengthen resilient supply chains, facilitate trade and investment, and leverage technology to drive development. He reaffirmed India’s support for the adoption of an Action Plan for the Multilateral Trade and Economic Cooperation Programme for the period 2026-2030.

national_raw_news.title: Asian Para Games 2026: India wins 30 medals, including Seven gold 5 hours ago 134
national_raw_news.content: India continued its strong performance at the Asian Para Games in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, today, as India’s medal tally has risen to 30, including seven gold, ten silver and thirteen bronze. India’s Pranav Soorma won gold in the men’s discus throw F51/52/53 event, scoring 932 points and also setting a new Asian record of 11.66 metres in the F51 event, while Ram Ratan Singh clinched silver with a throw of 10.35 metres, scoring 809 points in the same event. In the Women’s 200m T12 final, Simran clinched gold, clocking 24.80 seconds, setting a new Games record. Tejalben Damor also secured bronze, clocking 25.23 seconds in the same event. Indian para-athlete Deepthi Jeevanji won gold in the women’s 400-metre T20 event, setting a new Games record with a time of 56.36 seconds. In Powerlifting, Ashok won silver in the men’s 65-kilogram category with a lift of 192 kilograms. Shooter Manish Narwal also secured silver in the men’s 10-metre air pistol SH1 event, scoring 233.7 points. Shrishti Arora won bronze in the women’s 10-metre air pistol SH1 event, marking an impressive debut at the Games. In the javelin throw, Pradeep Kumar won silver with a personal best throw of 27.45 metres, while Ayush Verma claimed bronze with a throw of 17.88 metres. Swimmer Himanshu Nandal won bronze in the men’s 400-metre freestyle S11 event, clocking 5 minutes and 10.91 seconds to finish third. India also won five bronze medals in para table tennis today. Jehan Dorab Madan won bronze in the Men’s Singles Class 1 event after losing 3-nil to South Korean Kim Hyeonuk. Baby Sahana Ravi also secured bronze in the women’s singles Class 9 event, while Prachi Pandey secured bronze in the women’s singles Class 6 event. Bhavina Patel secured bronze after facing a 3-nil defeat to China’s Zhang Bian in the Women’s Singles Class 4-5 semi-finals. Sonalben Patel also secured a bronze in the women’s singles Class 3 event after losing her semi-final against South Korea’s Yoon Jiyu in straight games. In Para Archery, India has assured itself of at least five medals, with three Indian pairs reaching their respective finals. The recurve men’s pair of Harvinder Singh and Vijay Sundi, the recurve women’s pair of Bhawna and Pooja, and the compound women’s pair of Sheetal Devi and Payal Nag advanced to their gold medal match. In the individual events, Swati Chaudhary became the first Indian woman W1 archer to reach the final, while Sheetal Devi advanced to the women’s compound final.

national_raw_news.title: Manipur Police apprehend three suspects in connection with Nongshum civilian killings 43 mins ago 15
national_raw_news.content: Manipur Police have apprehended three suspects to be involved in Monday’s Nongshum incident in which three civilians were killed while the other three sustained bullet injuries when the victims went to collect firewood. Addressing a press conference at Police Headquarters in Imphal this evening, Additional Director General of Police (ADGP), Manipur, Lhari Dorjee Lhatoo, said that a joint team of security forces comprising Manipur Police, Indian Army, Assam Rifles and CRPF Cobra conducted a search operation around the incident place. The team apprehended three persons this morning in connection with the killing of three woodcutters at Nongshum Hills. The ADGP said that two of the arrested had admitted to being members of the assault team which is responsible for killing three civilians and injuring others, while the role of the third person is being investigated. He said that during the operation 12 sophisticated firearms, including INSAS rifles, AK-47, M-16, Sniper rifles, Type 81 rifles, hand grenades, Pompi bombs, over one thousand rounds of live ammunition, poppy plant seeds, radio sets and explosives were recovered. The ADGP appealed to the public to remain calm, exercise restraint and refrain from spreading rumours or unverified information on social media and urged to cooperate with security forces in maintaining peace and preventing violence.

national_raw_news.title: Indian Railways inaugurates new broad gauge lines in Chhattisgarh; flags off new train services from Raipur 2 hours ago 52
national_raw_news.content: Indian Railways today inaugurated the Tadoki-Rowghat and Abhanpur-Kurud broad gauge lines in Chattisgarh and flagged off new passenger train services connecting Raipur to Rowghat and Kurud. The arrival of a train at Raoghat for the first time since Independence marks a historic milestone in connecting the remote southern regions of the state to the national rail grid. The foundation stone for an electric locomotive maintenance facility was also laid in Raipur. The events were held in the presence of Chief Minister Vishnu Deo Sai and Railway Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw, who joined via video conferencing. The 95-km Dalli-Rajhara-Rowghat line, completed for 1,628 crore rupees, reached full operational status with the 17.5-km Tadoki-Raoghat stretch. Railway Minister Vaishnaw congratulated the people of Chhattisgarh and listed key ongoing and completed works, including the Dalli-Rajhara-Rowghat line, gauge conversion of the Kendi-Abhanpur-Rajim-Dhamtari section, multi-tracking projects and the recently approved Pendra Road-Bilaspur-Uslapur third line. The Kharsia-Parmalkasa double-line work is also in progress. Chief Minister Vishnu Deo Sai thanked Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Railway Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw on behalf of the state’s three crore people. He said, these projects, will give fresh impetus to industrial, commercial and socio-economic growth in remote areas. The Chief Minister said, services will improve connectivity in the Bastar region and boost trade, commerce, healthcare and education.
